learn.hook: Fractions live between the whole numbers on the number line. Let's go and find their homes!
points: A fraction names equal parts of a whole: 3/4 means 3 of 4 equal parts.
To show 3/4 on a number line, split the gap from 0 to 1 into 4 equal parts and take 3 jumps.
A fraction with a top bigger than the bottom, like 5/4, is more than 1. It lies between 1 and 2.
5/4 can be written as the mixed number 1 1/4 (one whole and one quarter).
Unit fractions get smaller as the bottom number grows: 1/2 > 1/3 > 1/4, because the whole is cut into more pieces.

example.q: Where does 7/3 lie on the number line?
steps: 3 thirds make 1 whole, 6 thirds make 2 wholes.
So it lies between 2 and 3, one third of the way from 2.

learn.reallife: Recipes ask for 1 1/2 cups of rice, and running tracks are split into quarter laps.

quiz.q: The gap from 0 to 1 is split into 5 equal parts. Riya lands on the 3rd mark after 0. Which fraction is she on?
quiz.explain: Each part is 1/5, and 3 jumps of 1/5 make 3/5.
quiz.mistake: Flips the fraction (5/3) or uses the mark number as the bottom

quiz.q: Which is larger: 1/6 or 1/9?
quiz.explain: Cutting a whole into 6 parts gives bigger pieces than cutting it into 9 parts. So 1/6 > 1/9.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a bigger bottom number means a bigger fraction

quiz.q: Write 13/4 as a mixed number.
quiz.explain: 13 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 1, so 13/4 = 3 wholes and 1/4.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the numbers around (4 1/3) or writes the remainder wrongly

quiz.q: Arjun ran 2 3/5 km. Write this as an improper fraction.
quiz.explain: 2 wholes = 10 fifths. Add 3 fifths: 13/5.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits side by side (23/5) or forgets the 3 fifths (10/5)

quiz.q: Between which two whole numbers does 17/5 lie?
quiz.explain: 17 ÷ 5 = 3 remainder 2, so 17/5 = 3 2/5, which lies between 3 and 4.
quiz.mistake: Looks at only the top number (17)

quiz.q: On a number line, each whole is split into quarters. How many jumps of 1/4 does it take to reach 1 1/2 from 0?
quiz.explain: 1 whole is 4 quarters and 1/2 is 2 quarters, so 1 1/2 = 6 quarters: 6 jumps.
quiz.mistake: Counts the 1 as one jump, or counts halves instead of quarters (3)

quiz.q: Kabir shares 3 rotis equally among 4 friends. What fraction of a roti does each friend get?
quiz.explain: 3 rotis shared by 4 means 3 ÷ 4 = 3/4 of a roti each.
steps: Cut each roti into 4 quarters: 12 quarters
quiz.mistake: Divides the wrong way round (4/3)

quiz.q: Which fraction is exactly equal to 1?
quiz.explain: 7/7 means all 7 of 7 equal parts, which is one whole. 7/1 is 7 wholes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 7/1 is one whole

teach.ask: Gappu hops on a number line: 'Where do I land for 3/4? It's not a whole number!'
teach.praise: Tweet! Split 0 to 1 into 4 equal parts and hop 3 times. I landed on 3/4!
teach.nudge: How should I cut up the gap from 0 to 1, and how many hops do I take?

learn.hook: Half a pizza or two quarters? Same amount of pizza, different names!
points: Equivalent fractions name the same amount: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8.
Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number to get an equivalent fraction: 2/3 = 8/12 (both × 4).
A fraction is in lowest terms when the top and bottom have no common factor except 1: 12/18 = 2/3 (both ÷ 6).
To compare fractions, change them to the same denominator: 2/3 = 8/12 and 3/4 = 9/12, so 3/4 is bigger.
Adding the same number to top and bottom does NOT give an equivalent fraction.

steps: The greatest common factor of 18 and 24 is 6

learn.reallife: When you cut a cake into 8 slices and eat 4, you've eaten half, just as if it were cut into 2 and you ate 1.

items.text: Multiply the top and bottom by the ___ number to get an equivalent fraction.

quiz.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 3/4?
quiz.explain: Multiply the top and bottom of 3/4 by 3: 9/12.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies only the bottom (3/8) or only the top

quiz.q: Write 24/36 in lowest terms.
quiz.explain: The greatest common factor of 24 and 36 is 12. 24 ÷ 12 = 2 and 36 ÷ 12 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Divides top and bottom by different numbers

quiz.q: Meena ate 2/8 of a pizza. Harpreet ate 1/4 of the same-sized pizza. Who ate more?
quiz.explain: 2/8 in lowest terms is 1/4, so they ate the same amount.
quiz.mistake: Thinks bigger numbers in the fraction mean more pizza

quiz.q: Which is bigger: 5/6 or 7/9?
quiz.explain: With denominator 18: 5/6 = 15/18 and 7/9 = 14/18. So 5/6 is bigger.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the fraction with bigger numbers is bigger

quiz.q: Fill in the missing number: 4/7 = 20/?
quiz.explain: 4 × 5 = 20, so multiply the bottom by 5 too: 7 × 5 = 35.
quiz.mistake: Adds 20 to the bottom (27) or multiplies the bottom by 4 instead of 5 (28)

quiz.q: Aisha says 2/5 = 4/7 because she added 2 to the top and to the bottom. What is wrong?
options: She should add 2 only to the top
We must multiply or divide top and bottom by the same number, not add
quiz.explain: 2/5 = 4/10 (both × 2). Adding the same number changes the amount: 4/7 is bigger than 2/5.
quiz.mistake: Thinks adding the same number to top and bottom keeps a fraction equal

quiz.q: Which is the smallest: 1/2, 2/3, 3/8 or 5/12?
quiz.mistake: Picks the fraction with the smallest top number without comparing properly

quiz.q: A chocolate bar has 12 equal pieces. Joseph eats 9 pieces. What fraction did he eat, in lowest terms?
quiz.explain: He ate 9/12. Divide top and bottom by 3: 3/4.
quiz.mistake: Gives the part left over (1/4) instead of the part eaten

teach.ask: Gappu is puzzled: 'How can 1/2 and 3/6 be equal? The numbers are different!'
teach.praise: Chirp chirp! 1/2 × 3 on top and bottom gives 3/6. Same amount of mango, just cut smaller!
teach.nudge: What can I do to the top and bottom numbers without changing the amount?

learn.hook: Half a glass of lassi plus a quarter glass: how full is the glass? Let's add fractions!
points: Same denominator: add or subtract the tops and keep the bottom. 2/7 + 3/7 = 5/7.
Different denominators: first change to equivalent fractions with a common denominator. 1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6.
Never add the bottoms! 1/2 + 1/2 is 1, not 2/4.
Mixed numbers: change to improper fractions first, or add the wholes and the parts separately.
Brahmagupta, an Indian mathematician who lived about 1400 years ago, wrote down rules for working with fractions like these.
learn.reallife: Cooking with 1/2 cup and 1/4 cup, or adding up pieces of a shared pizza, uses fraction addition.

games.title: Fraction sums: true or false?
items: Same denominator, so add the tops: 3 + 1 = 4.
To add 1/4 and 1/6 you can use 12 as a common denominator.
12 is a multiple of both 4 and 6.

quiz.q: Riya drinks 2/9 of a bottle of lassi in the morning and 4/9 in the evening. How much does she drink in all?
quiz.explain: 2/9 + 4/9 = 6/9, which is 2/3 in lowest terms.
quiz.mistake: Adds the bottoms too (6/18)
Adds tops and bottoms separately (2/7)

quiz.q: A ribbon is 7/8 m long. Kabir cuts off 3/8 m. How much ribbon is left?
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting (10/8)

quiz.explain: 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12, so the difference is 1/12.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts tops and bottoms separately (1/1)

quiz.q: Arjun walks 1 1/2 km to school and then 2 1/4 km to the market. How far does he walk in total?
quiz.mistake: Adds the fraction parts by adding tops and bottoms (2/6)

quiz.q: Mother made 1 whole cake. 2/5 was eaten at lunch and 1/3 at tea time. What fraction is left?
quiz.mistake: Gives the part eaten (11/15) instead of the part left

quiz.q: What is the right first step for 2/3 + 1/4?
options: Add tops and bottoms to get 3/7
quiz.explain: 12 is a common multiple of 3 and 4. Then 8/12 + 3/12 = 11/12.
quiz.mistake: Adds the denominators to make a 'common' denominator

quiz.q: Meena says 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/8. What is the correct answer?
quiz.explain: Keep the denominator: 1/4 + 1/4 = 2/4 = 1/2. (2/8 is only 1/4, which would mean the sum is no bigger than one part!)
quiz.mistake: Adds the denominators as well as the numerators

teach.ask: Gappu ate 1/2 a guava and then 1/3 of another one: 'How much guava did I eat altogether?'
teach.praise: Tweet! Change both to sixths: 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6. I ate 5/6 of a guava. Yum!
teach.nudge: Can I add halves and thirds straight away, or do the pieces need to be the same size first?
